interactions.summary: The class debates whether the nighttime rule has been transcended, but Jiang pivots into character psychology: Dante has been lingering because he is infatuated with his own shadow, and Beatrice's frustration supplies a motive for Lucia's intervention.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led exchange with several student proposals

claims.claim: Jiang floats a practical reading that Dante may have simply overslept into daytime, so Lucia's intervention comes after he has stalled rather than as a direct violation of the night rule.

Jiang reframes the whole episode as narrative psychology: Dante is moving slowly because he has become enamored of his own shadow, lingering with the shades and procrastinating instead of pressing toward Beatrice.

In Jiang's reading, Beatrice is angry because Dante has shifted his attention from her to his own shadow, so Lucia's carrying intervention becomes a corrective act of love rather than arbitrary plot machinery.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns Dante's delay into vanity theater: he is in love with his own shadow, dawdling among admirers while Beatrice watches from above.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he's in love with his shadow
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It converts a technical plot question into a sharp moral-psychological diagnosis of Dante's current state.

signature_moments.moment: The imagined scene of Dante offering autographs in anti-Purgatory makes Lucia's intervention feel like a rescue from spiritual procrastination, not a lazy shortcut.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang uses comic exaggeration to explain why grace might forcibly move Dante along.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture departs from structural explanations of the gate transition and lands on a character diagnosis: Dante's slowed ascent comes from self-absorption, which higher love must interrupt.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang marks the oversleeping explanation as his own interpretation rather than an explicit statement of the poem, so it should remain a dated classroom reading.
